requirements.evidence: Contract signatures match task.md (CreateQueue.php:26, UpdateQueue.php:25, SetQueueAccess.php:29); name is trimmed and the slug is derived/slugified, unique per entity, with a unique-index race converted to ValidationException (CreateQueue.php:28-59, UpdateQueue.php:32-61); no delete action exists; Ticket::call locks, rejects inactive, authorizes, then checks waiting (Ticket.php:97-123); audit grant/revoke carries actor_id, queue_id, entity_membership_id and a revoke is only logged when a row was deleted (SetQueueAccess.php:50-74).

conventions.evidence: Domain writes are in app/Actions and authorize inside (CreateQueue.php:28, UpdateQueue.php:32, SetQueueAccess.php:35); authorization is centralized in one policy (QueuePolicy.php:22-73); the migration is a reversible, generated-style file (database/migrations/2026_10_29_032547_create_queue_access_table.php:15-31); mass assignment is guarded with #[Fillable] (QueueAccess.php:11); Pest tests plus the required docs/CHANGELOG updates are present (change.diff:9, 665-691, 704-722).

security.evidence: Authorization runs before any write in all three actions (CreateQueue.php:28, UpdateQueue.php:32, SetQueueAccess.php:35); both call paths use QueuePolicy (CallNextTicket.php:39, Ticket.php:119); permissions are validated as a list of enum values (SetQueueAccess.php:37-40) and a corrupted non-array permissions value denies (QueuePolicy.php:65-67); no unescaped output or client-trusted values are introduced.

tests.evidence: New Pest suites cover the actions, policy, model and factory (tests/Feature/Queue/CreateQueueTest.php:15, UpdateQueueTest.php:19, SetQueueAccessTest.php:28, QueuePolicyTest.php:15); unauthorized paths are tested (CreateQueueTest.php:132, UpdateQueueTest.php:142, SetQueueAccessTest.php:118); slug races are simulated (CreateQueueTest.php:68-95, UpdateQueueTest.php:90-111); both call paths get unauthorized/corrupted-permission coverage (CallNextTicketTest.php:256, IssueTicketTest.php:182).

simplicity.evidence: Three small single-purpose actions; the existing unique-violation check was extracted once into DatabaseErrors::isUniqueViolation (DatabaseErrors.php:14) and reused instead of duplicated (CreateQueue.php:53, UpdateQueue.php:61, IssueTicket.php:57); QueueAccessFactory's states reuse the existing model factories (QueueAccessFactory.php:34-51); no service/repository layer or speculative abstraction was added.

readability.evidence: PHPDoc states the contract and @throws for each action (CreateQueue.php:19-25, UpdateQueue.php:18-24, SetQueueAccess.php:20-28); methods are short with domain-revealing names (QueuePolicy.php:69 isManagerOf); the queue-then-ticket lock order is documented (Ticket.php:84-87); style matches the sibling actions and factories.

scope.evidence: The diff is limited to the queue actions/policy/model/migration/factory, the two authorized call paths, tests, docs and CHANGELOG; the only pre-existing production file touched beyond the call paths is IssueTicket.php, solely to share the unique-violation helper (change.diff:119-154); no UI, extra permissions or delete action was added.

issues.explanation: The race test calls Queue::flushEventListeners() in its finally block, which removes every Queue model listener for the rest of the Pest process, not only the listener registered by the test, so later tests can become order-dependent or lose Queue observer behaviour.

isUniqueViolation() returns true for any SQLSTATE 23000 (which also covers foreign-key and other integrity errors), so a genuine database failure in the two new actions would be reported to callers as a duplicate-slug ValidationException instead of surfacing the real error.

review.summary: Implements the full queue-management and call-authorization slice: CreateQueue/UpdateQueue/SetQueueAccess, the queue_access table/model/factory, QueuePermission and a single QueuePolicy wired into both ticket-call paths, with doc/CHANGELOG updates and a broad Pest suite covering race, cross-entity and corrupted-permission cases. Requirements and security are met; only minor test-hygiene and error-classification nits remain, so the PR is approvable with nits.
